title: ok cancel default vs explicit verb
name: OK/Cancel default vs explicit verb — Ant
rule: OK / Cancel as Ant default labels (CONFLICT). Spec still defaults to OK/Cancel but also: use a verb; describe the result (Publish, Login); if primary is negative, stress consequences (Delete / Cancel). Dual-cite vs NN/g `explicit_verb_not_ok`. Do not pick a winner. Prefer cited verb-names-the-outcome as pass when both apply; Ant default is a conflict flag, not a second invented rule.
pass_when: When both cites apply, the primary names the outcome (Publish, Login, Delete); if primary is negative, the pair stresses consequences (Delete / Cancel).
fail_when: Generic OK where a specific verb is available and treated as satisfying the verb-names cite; or a house "always OK/Cancel" / "never OK" that deletes the other cite.
overview: Ant defaults OK/Cancel yet also asks verbs that name the outcome.
apply_when: Labeling dialog or form primary and cancel actions under Ant.
not_when: House rules that always ban OK or always require OK/Cancel only.
agent_hint: Prefer a verb that names the outcome; flag OK/Cancel as the Ant conflict.
